description: Top-level wireframe editor component. Renders through the core TmEditorShell: an optional header (host slots HeaderStart / HeaderActions / Title), ONE command row (a core TmToolbar with named groups - tools, history, arrange, group, align, snap, zoom, file -, per-button Priority, Labels=Auto and Overflow=Menu; Export is the primary, never-collapsing action; the format painter, Read-only, rulers and the panel toggles live in its "More" menu), a docked left panel (Components / Pages / Layers tabs, Pages only with PageNavigation=Panel), the canvas with rulers, context menu and minimap, and an inspector (Canvas with device presets, Page and Grid sections on an empty selection; Element with a Name field and Delete element on a selection). Creates and owns a WireframeCommandStack (undo/redo) and exposes it to all child components via CascadingValue. Supports JSON import/export, SVG export, zoom, grid, read-only mode and collapsible panels. Tool mode (Select/Pan) can be switched via toolbar buttons or keyboard shortcuts V/H. Canvas size is edited in the inspector (Canvas section). There is no built-in Save or Open: the host supplies them through the header slots. Presentation: every colour, radius and space reads a core --tm-* token through the --tm-wd-* aliases (no local palette, no dark-mode block), so dark mode and the indigo theme work without extra CSS; toolbar buttons are TmIcon (32px; 44px on a coarse pointer). Responsive behaviour follows the editor's own container width (see LayoutMode): desktop docks the panels, a tablet uses a two-row toolbar and one side sheet at a time, and a phone (container below 768 px, decision G2: viewing + light edits) shows a compact header (title + host slots) with a select / pan / undo / redo / More tool row, a full-width canvas with a floating zoom pill, a TmMobileActionBar (Components, Pages & layers, Export, More; host actions through MobileActions) and non-modal bottom sheets (peek / half / full) for the palette, the Properties inspector (type + Duplicate / Lock / Delete on peek, Name and every property on half) and the Pages | Layers segment. Selecting, moving an element with a finger, undo / redo, tap-insert, layers, device presets, export and the long-press action sheet stay; resize / rotate handles, rubber band, edge drawing, align / distribute, grouping, rulers, minimap and JSON import are tablet and up. The export dialog is a bottom sheet on a phone.

parameters.name: Document
parameters.description: Document being edited. Bind with @bind-Document. When null an empty document is created automatically.

parameters.name: DocumentChanged
parameters.description: Raised after every mutation so callers can persist the document.

parameters.name: ReadOnly
parameters.description: Host-pinned read-only mode: prevents all editing interactions (drag, resize, drop, prop changes, toolbox insertion). Never assigned by the component - the built-in Read-only/Edit toggle drives an internal user state (IsReadOnly = ReadOnly || user toggle) and reports it through ReadOnlyChanged. While ReadOnly=true is pinned and ReadOnlyChanged is not bound the toggle is not rendered, so the editor cannot be unlocked from the UI; use @bind-ReadOnly to follow and own the state.

parameters.name: ReadOnlyChanged
parameters.description: Raised with the new effective read-only state when the user flips the Read-only/Edit toggle. Binding it (@bind-ReadOnly) keeps the toggle available while the host value is true.

parameters.name: ShowToolbox
parameters.description: Show the component toolbox: the Components tab of the left panel. When no tab is left (no toolbox, no Layers, no Pages) the left panel is not rendered. Collapsing the panel is shell state (the strip toggle or the Components panel entry in the More menu).

parameters.name: ShowPropertiesPanel
parameters.description: Show the right-hand inspector. false also hides the Layers tab of the left panel (the two lived together in the right column before the shell restructure). Collapsing the inspector is shell state (the strip toggle or the Properties panel entry in the More menu).

parameters.name: ShowMinimap
parameters.description: Show the minimap overlay in the bottom-right corner of the canvas.

parameters.name: ShowToolbar
parameters.description: Show the command row (the core TmToolbar: tools, history, arrange, grouping, alignment, snapping, zoom, export/import) and, unless a header is shown, the document title.

parameters.name: ShowGrid
parameters.description: Initial / host-driven visibility of the grid lines. Never assigned by the component - the inspector's Grid section flips an internal state and reports it through ShowGridChanged (@bind-ShowGrid).

parameters.name: ShowGridChanged
parameters.description: Raised with the new value when the user toggles the grid in the inspector (use @bind-ShowGrid).

parameters.name: GridSize
parameters.description: Initial / host-driven snap-to-grid cell size in pixels; 0 disables snapping. Never assigned by the component - the inspector's Grid section changes an internal value and reports it through GridSizeChanged (@bind-GridSize).

parameters.name: GridSizeChanged
parameters.description: Raised with the new cell size when the user edits the grid size in the inspector (use @bind-GridSize).

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class applied to the editor root element.

parameters.name: ShowPageTabs
parameters.description: Show the page navigation (the horizontal page tabs, or the Pages tab of the left panel with PageNavigation=Panel), even when there is only one page.

parameters.name: PageNavigation
parameters.description: Where the pages are presented. Tabs (default) keeps the horizontal page tabs above the canvas (Components and Layers tabs in the left panel); Panel adds a Pages tab (TmWireframePagesPanel) to the left panel and drops the horizontal tabs.

parameters.name: LayoutMode
parameters.description: How the editor resolves its layout: Auto (default) measures the editor's own container (not the viewport) against LayoutBreakpoints and sets data-editor-layout on the root; a forced mode pins the presentation (tests, host layouts). Desktop (container >= 1200) docks the left panel and the inspector in the shell, with one toolbar and the minimap card. Tablet (768-1199) renders a two-row toolbar split by group (editing commands, then panel toggles / zoom / Export / Import), the left panel (Components / Pages / Layers) as an overlay drawer and the inspector as a non-modal side sheet with a close button - at most ONE sheet open, selecting an element opens the inspector, inserting a component closes the drawer, Escape closes the sheet and returns the focus to the canvas -, no minimap, a single-column toolbox and 44px targets on a coarse pointer. Mobile (< 768) uses the shell sheet presentation.

parameters.name: LayoutBreakpoints
parameters.description: Per-instance layout thresholds for the editor container. null uses the editor default: mobile below 768 (TmBreakpoints.Md), desktop from 1200, tablet in between.

parameters.name: ShowHeader
parameters.description: Show the shell header row. false (default) keeps the pre-shell look: the title sits at the start of the toolbar row and no header renders - unless a host supplies HeaderStart, HeaderActions or Title, which opens the header on its own.

parameters.name: HeaderStart
parameters.description: Host content at the start of the header, before the title (G9 slot). The editor has no built-in Save or Open.

parameters.name: HeaderActions
parameters.description: Host content at the end of the header, after the title (G9 slot) - e.g. an Open... or Save button.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: Host content that replaces the built-in editable document title (G9 slot). Opens the header like HeaderStart.

parameters.name: ShowRulers
parameters.description: Initial / host-driven visibility of the rulers around the canvas. Never assigned by the component - the toolbar toggle flips an internal state and reports it through ShowRulersChanged; a later change of the parameter value is adopted again.

parameters.name: ShowRulersChanged
parameters.description: Raised with the new value when the user toggles the rulers button (@bind-ShowRulers).

parameters.name: ComponentScope
parameters.description: Optional application scope used to resolve custom wireframe components.

parameters.name: MobileActions
parameters.description: Host actions of the mobile action bar (editor container below 768 px, decision G2: viewing + light edits). The built-in tiles - Components, Pages & layers, Export - come first; a host action pinned ActionOverflow.Never (for example "Save") keeps a tile of its own, the others join the "More" menu by their rank. There is no built-in Save or Open: hosts supply them here and in HeaderStart / HeaderActions. Ignored on a tablet or desktop layout.

cssVariables.name: --tm-wd-accent
cssVariables.description: Accent (selection, active button, handles). Alias of --tm-color-primary; follows the default blue, the opt-in indigo theme (data-tm-theme="indigo") and dark mode.

cssVariables.name: --tm-wd-bg-surface
cssVariables.description: Toolbar, panel and dialog surface. Alias of --tm-bg-surface.

cssVariables.name: --tm-wd-border
cssVariables.description: Hairlines and control borders. Alias of --tm-border-color.

cssVariables.name: --tm-wd-canvas-surface
cssVariables.description: Workspace behind the page. Alias of --tm-bg-workspace (indigo off-white / dark slate).

cssVariables.name: --tm-wd-canvas-bg
cssVariables.description: The wireframe PAGE. Alias of the theme-invariant --tm-paper: wireframe components are drawn light-on-paper, so the page stays paper in dark mode and the SVG/PNG/PDF export matches the screen.

cssVariables.name: --tm-wd-grid-minor
cssVariables.description: Minor grid step (drawn at 55% opacity). Alias of --tm-paper-border.

cssVariables.name: --tm-wd-sheet-w
cssVariables.description: Width of the tablet side sheets (the left drawer and the inspector): 20rem, capped at 60% of the canvas region. Replaces the former fixed --tm-wd-toolbox-w / --tm-wd-props-w.

examples.title: Basic wireframe editor with two-way binding
Editor without grid, custom canvas size
Pages as a left-panel tab, host Open action in the header
Persist document to server on every change
examples.code:
<TmWireframeEditor @bind-Document="_document"
                   DocumentChanged="SaveAsync" />

@code {
    private WireframeDocument _document = new();

    private async Task SaveAsync(WireframeDocument doc)
    {
        var json = WireframeSerializer.Serialize(doc);
        await Http.PutAsJsonAsync("api/wireframes/my-doc", json);
    }
}
